key_insight: Language models exhibit nonlinear dynamics across three clocks—layer depth, training steps, and token generation—with repetition-loop escape following an Arrhenius law.
engineering_relevance: Dynamical-systems models offer interpretable tools for studying training stability and generation temperature, though adaptive loop control has not yet outperformed the best fixed temperature.
method: Synthesize about 200 papers into a Three-Clock Dictionary mapping 15 concepts, with correspondences labeled proved, measured, or conjectured.
Derive reduced-order models linking softmax, gradient descent, attention, and repetition to physical dynamics.
Test predictions on open language models and a small transformer using a laptop CPU.
evidence_signal: GPT-2 and Pythia experiments support Arrhenius repetition-loop escape with logit-gap barriers; Pythia layers become more expansive during training, and a small transformer trains at a multi-mode edge of stability.
watch_item: The framework mixes established results with conjectures, and loop-removal controllers do not yet beat the best fixed-temperature baseline.
paper_title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
